column1: # HOW THIS WAS PRODUCED
# Read: finding-gate/README.md (Layout, case.json, Surfaces, Verdicts sections);
# scripts/finding-gate/RenameMaps.php in full (class docblock lines ~1-130,
# SURFACES/FILES/PREFIXES/IMAGE_SEPARATOR constants, buildSubstitutions() lines
# 582-711, assertPlainMetricKey() ~995-1013, assertReportValueSpelling() ~1021-1062,
# assertWholeInputToken() ~1063-1093, assertNoSuffixOverlap() ~1233-1290);
# scripts/finding-gate/MetricVocabulary.php in full (assertSuffixesAgreeWith()
# ~91-105, the class docblock's own measured figures);
# docs/internal/plans/rule-vocabulary/FOLLOWUPS.md, section "Ш5e3-0 — the gate's
# key-map tooling" (the claim under test);
# `head -1` and current contents of all five finding-gate/maps/*.tsv (all empty
# — no step is mid-flight on this branch).
# No code was executed for this file: RenameMaps.php's load-time assertions
# were read, not driven with a crafted row, because reproducing them needs a
# populated maps/ directory plus two checked-out trees (candidate + reference)
# and this branch carries neither yet (X11 is preparation, not the rename
# step). Every claim below cites the exact assertion in the source rather than
# an observed refusal message.
# WHAT THIS METHOD DOES NOT SEE
# - Whether the code changes shape once a real step populates the maps and
#   runs the gate for real — this is a static read of scripts/finding-gate/ as
#   of 2026-09-07, same as FOLLOWUPS.md's own entry was as of 2026-08-26.
# - `declared-delta.tsv` / `declared-field-moves.tsv` / `normalization.tsv` /
#   `equivalence-tuple.tsv` — the brief named five maps in `finding-gate/maps/`
#   specifically; these four other tracked files in `finding-gate/` are a
#   different declaration mechanism (structural deltas, field moves, compared-
#   field exclusions) and are out of scope for "map row shapes".
# - Whether a hand-run of the gate with a real populated `metric-keys.tsv` and
#   two live trees would surface a code path this reading missed; that would
#   need an actual rename step to exist.
# ANSWER TO THE BRIEF'S QUESTION: is there a row shape that declares a rename
# of an AGGREGATION SUFFIX (`.avg`, `.sum`, `.p5`, ...) itself?
# No such shape exists in today's code, and FOLLOWUPS.md's Ш5e3-0 claim is
# RE-READ against the current HEAD of claude/x11-final-vocabulary, 2026-09-07:
# item 1 is CORRECTED — its 2026-08-26 wording named the wrong guard, and the
# refusal it describes turns out to rest on item 2 alone. Item 2 is confirmed
# unchanged since 2026-08-26.
#   1. `metric-keys.tsv` is WRITTEN for a plain base key on each side, and its
#      load-time check does not enforce that shape — corrected 2026-09-07,
#      read against the code rather than against its own error text.
#      `assertPlainMetricKey()` (scripts/finding-gate/RenameMaps.php:995-1013)
#      matches `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, and that pattern ADMITS a dot:
#      `complexity.ccn.avg` passes it. What the check really refuses is `#` and
#      `:` — the channel-pair and rule-option separators — which is what keeps
#      a metric-keys half from being a channel or a selector spelling; its
#      message ('"%s" is not a plain metric key. A metric-keys row is expanded
#      over the aggregation suffixes, and "<that>.<strategy>" is a spelling no
#      surface carries.') names a shape the pattern does not actually exclude.
#      So a suffixed row CAN be written and does load. It buys nothing: the row
#      is itself expanded over the suffixes, so a `<key>.<strategy>` half only
#      ever produces `<key>.<strategy>.<strategy>` spellings, which no surface
#      carries — the rubber stamp the check exists to refuse, arrived at by
#      matching nothing instead of by refusing. The refusal of an
#      aggregation-suffix STEP is therefore SINGLE-mechanism, and the mechanism
#      is item 2's `assertSuffixesAgreeWith()`, which stops the gate before any
#      row is consulted.
#   2. The suffix list a `metric-keys.tsv` row IS expanded over comes from
#      `MetricVocabulary::ofTree()`, read as a closed, ordered list of
#      `AggregationStrategy` case values from each of the two checked-out
#      trees (scripts/finding-gate/MetricVocabulary.php:63-68). The candidate's
#      list and the reference's list are compared for exact equality by
#      `assertSuffixesAgreeWith()` (MetricVocabulary.php:91-105), and the gate
#      REFUSES TO RUN AT ALL — throws `GateError`, before any comparison is
#      attempted — the moment they differ: 'The two trees do not agree on the
#      aggregation suffixes a metric key may carry ... the gate has no shape to
#      declare that in — so it stops here rather than comparing a translation
#      it cannot state.' A step that renames, adds, or removes a suffix makes
#      the two trees' lists differ by construction, so this refusal fires
#      unconditionally for such a step; there is no map row that could satisfy
#      it, because the check runs before any row is consulted.
#   3. `assertNoSuffixOverlap()` (RenameMaps.php:1233-1290) is a separate,
#      narrower load-time check (collision between a declared key's expanded
#      `<key>.<strategy>` spellings and another declared name) and likewise
#      offers no row shape for a suffix rename — it only ever iterates
#      `$this->vocabulary->suffixes` to EXPAND an already-plain key, never to
#      compare or translate a suffix spelling itself.
# Net: the refusal is structural (a load-time equality assertion over two
# read-only closed lists), not a missing row TYPE that could be added to
# `metric-keys.tsv` without also changing `MetricVocabulary` and
# `assertPlainMetricKey`'s invariant. FOLLOWUPS.md is accurate as written and
# needs no update from this reading.
map
channels.tsv
column2: one whole channel key -> one whole channel key (old, new, reason); forward-only (RenameMaps.php:31-38); the `ruleName#violationCode` pair form is accepted as a whole-key spelling too, since Ш5b a channel carries one name (finding-gate/README.md "A claim is a channel@level pair")
column3: every surface a bare channel code reaches: all 12 report formats' code/ruleId/check_name/source fields, the baseline file's "channel" field, `bin/qmx rules`, `baseline:explain`, and — via the `qmx.` PREFIXES constant (RenameMaps.php ~180) — Checkstyle's prefixed `source` attribute; also a case's own `--rule-opt`/`--disable-rule`/`suppress_*` CLI and config input, via the shared substitution machinery, WHEN the same name is separately declared with an `inputs.tsv` role (RenameMaps.php:88-97, the "two roles, one declaration" rule)
column4: a rename of a channel's LEVEL alone (level comes from the `subject` tag, not the name, per README's "Coverage counts pairs" section) — that is `case.json`'s hand-written `channels` claim's job, not this map's; a collapse/split that is not a clean bijection is expressed by MULTIPLE rows (one old -> several new is a declared split, several old -> one new is a declared collapse), never by one row alone
column5: forward-only and never invertible even where it looks safe: a collapsed target name can collide with an unrelated corpus argument spelled identically, so the map is applied one direction only (RenameMaps.php:31-38)

column1: symbols.tsv
column2: one FQN or file path -> one FQN or file path (old, new, reason); the only map declared reversible in both directions (RenameMaps.php:170,262 FILES[self::SYMBOLS] = true), generated mechanically from `git diff --find-renames` per finding-gate/README.md
column3: subject identifiers embedded in findings/baseline entries (`declaration:callable:Old\Fqn::method@path`), and — because reversible — the reference's own CLI/config input when a case's fixture path or class name changed under the step
column4: a metric or channel rename riding along a symbol move — those are separate roles requiring their own row even if the symbol also carries a metric-like name (RenameMaps.php's "one name may hold two roles" section, ~row 85-97, describes the declared-merge escape hatch, but it is still a SEPARATE declaration, not implied by symbols.tsv)
column5: reversibility is checked, not assumed: `FILES` marks it invertible and the injectivity of the pair set is verified at load (class docblock, "A map may be applied backwards if and only if it is injective in both directions")

column1: metric-keys.tsv
column2: one PLAIN base metric key -> one PLAIN base metric key (old, new, reason); forward-only (RenameMaps.php:44-52); automatically re-applied to every `<key>.<strategy>` spelling for every suffix in the CLOSED, cross-tree-agreed `AggregationStrategy` list (RenameMaps.php:76-84, 651-663)
column3: matched only where quoted (`"<key>"`), never bare, and only on `format:json`, `format:metrics`, `format:html` (the SURFACES const, RenameMaps.php:163-165)
column4: a rename of the STRATEGY/SUFFIX vocabulary itself (`avg`, `sum`, `p5`, ...) — no row unit exists for it at all, see the header answer above; a bare (unquoted) occurrence of a key in prose — deliberately excluded, since half the vocabulary is ordinary English (`cognitive`, `distance`) and a bare substitution would corrupt message text (RenameMaps.php ~648-657, measured example quoted in the docblock)
column5: the two trees' suffix lists are asserted EQUAL before any row is even consulted (MetricVocabulary::assertSuffixesAgreeWith); a step that changes the suffix list cannot be run through the gate under any row content. That assertion is the ONLY thing stopping such a step: `assertPlainMetricKey()` (RenameMaps.php:995-1013) does NOT refuse a `<key>.<strategy>` half despite saying so — its pattern admits a dot, and what it actually excludes is `#` and `:` (corrected 2026-09-07; see header item 1). A suffixed half loads and then matches nothing, because the row is expanded over the suffixes a second time

column1: inputs.tsv
column2: option keys, flag aliases, and names inside selectors, as a document/CLI writes them; reversible (FILES[self::INPUTS] = true); UNIQUELY multivalued forward — one old token may list SEVERAL new tokens separated by `IMAGE_SEPARATOR` ('|', RenameMaps.php:198-203) — but only usable backwards (new -> old is a function; old -> new is not, so forward application of a multivalued row is refused rather than guessing the first image, RenameMaps.php:17-29)
column3: CLI/config input surfaces: `--rule-opt`, `--disable-rule`, `only_rules`/`disabled_rules`, selector-shaped config keys, and any other place a case argument spells a producer/channel/rule name it does not just publish
column4: arbitrary text mentioning a name in prose (same quoting/boundary rules as the other roles); and — like every map — a name that is a SUBSTRING of a longer declared name, refused by the whole-name boundary assertion (`assertWholeInputToken`, RenameMaps.php:1063-1093) rather than silently rewritten as a prefix
column5: a token whose forward image is ambiguous cannot be applied forwards at all — this is the one map where "cannot declare" is really "can declare, but only one direction of it fires"; the reverse (new -> old) is the direction the reference's own CLI/config args are translated in, since the reference cannot be handed a vocabulary it predates (class docblock lines 10-15)

column1: report-values.tsv
column2: one enumerable REPORT FIELD VALUE -> one new value (old, new, reason); forward-only, and for a different reason than channels/metric-keys: there is no backwards direction to check injectivity of in the first place, because no case argument ever addresses a report value on input (RenameMaps.php:52-58)
column3: matched only quoted, only on `format:suppressed` (the sole surface measured to publish such a value, SURFACES const)
column4: the POSITION/order of an enumerated value (a row states a value, never its ordinal — RenameMaps.php ~row 62-64); any value on a surface other than `format:suppressed` — an occurrence elsewhere is reported as an undeclared diff, not silently translated (measured-and-declared restriction, same paragraph)
column5: narrowest of the five maps by design: one surface, one field shape (quoted enumerable value), no suffix expansion of any kind — nothing analogous to metric-keys.tsv's aggregation-suffix machinery exists here because there is no aggregation concept for a report value
